questions.question: What should you do if the brake pedal does not build pressure?

options.text: Upshift.
Downshift.
Hold the brake pedal down as far as it will go.
Pump the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose pressure, shift to a lower gear. This will help slow down your vehicle.

questions.question: When coupling, you should:

options.text: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
Only couple one set of glad hands.
It is best to leave one glad hand loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts because:

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made to drive in wet weather.
The water has not yet absorbed the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface. This creates a slick film before the water washes it away.

questions.question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Make sudden steering moves.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.
Drive slowly around corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around corners.
questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk with a combination vehicle, keep the cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should:

options.text: Continue to drive.
Pull over and find out what is wrong.
Run the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and find out what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the safe level, stop driving as soon as possible. There may be a problem that could cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check that the cargo is secure every:

options.text: 10 miles.
150 miles.
500 miles.
1,000 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before starting a trip, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, the heaviest cargo should be placed:

options.text: On top of the lightest parts of the cargo.
Under the lightest parts of the cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under the lightest parts of the cargo.
questions.explanation: Keep your vehicle balanced to prevent rollover. Place heavy cargo underneath lighter cargo to keep weight low and centered.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, the driver should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to get them to move.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Special permits are needed for loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy. These loads may have driving restrictions.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:

options.text: Loose.
Free of oil.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil.
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose or soaked with oil or grease. They should not be dangerously thin.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
You are experiencing a trailer jackknife.
Wheels have regained traction after a skid.
Air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve will pop out if air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), how should you brake?

options.text: Brake harder than in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make ABS activate.
Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way whether your vehicle has ABS or not. ABS works automatically without changing how you should brake.

questions.question: What happens if you accelerate roughly?

options.text: It can damage the vehicle.
It is normal after warming up the engine.
It helps save fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration causes the vehicle to jerk and can damage it.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking fully.
Turn on one turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking fully.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Before coupling a second trailer, how should you secure it?

options.text: Empty its air tanks.
Lean it against a wall.
Remove its emergency line.
Place wheel chocks under the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place wheel chocks under the wheels.
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks to secure the trailer in place while you couple it. This is important if you are unsure about the trailer's brakes.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: ABS cannot work because of bad weather.
ABS has just started working.
ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: When the ABS warning light comes on, something is wrong with the Anti-Lock Braking System and it is not working as it should.

questions.question: Which one does NOT show bad brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Brake pads that are clean and dry
Brake shoes that are very thin

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn too thin. Clean, dry pads are a good sign.

questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner, what do the rear wheels do?

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.
Are not important for the driver to watch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a tighter path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have more off-tracking than shorter ones.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Look quickly and then back at the road.
Look at the mirrors for a long time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look quickly and then back at the road.
questions.explanation: Glance at mirrors briefly. Looking at them too long is dangerous because you stop watching the road ahead and travel a long distance without seeing what is in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do to drive more safely at night?

options.text: Keep the interior light on.
Dim the instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges.
Do not nap before driving.
Use only low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dim the instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges.
questions.explanation: Turn off the interior light and set the instrument lights to the lowest level where you can still read them. A bright cab makes it hard to see outside at night.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
The weight of the tire itself.
The weight of the air inside a fully inflated tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a certain air pressure. This information is printed on the side of the tire.
